groups.job: Put the uses of one ability back to full at the start of a new game session. The combat round counter has a button of its own that puts the round count back to the start; it is a different thing but the same kind of act.
groups.differences_carry_meaning: No. All seven session buttons give uses back for a new session (Kharmic Tie, Luck, Dark Paragon, Great Destiny, Haunted, Unlucky and the Ancestor card). The one round-counter "Reset" is a different job (it is not about sessions) but also puts a counter back to its start.
groups.why: It is the word the owner used for Kharmic Tie, it fits the one-row Kharmic Tie card on a phone (the reason for the question), and the card already shows which ability it belongs to. The spoken name still says "for a new session", so nothing is lost for a screen reader. The round counter’s "Reset" then already matches.
other_words_offered: Reset session (keep, and rename the round counter to "Reset rounds")

groups.job: Open a window or a list again so a choice you already made can be changed (or made, the first time).
groups.differences_carry_meaning: Partly. "Choose…" (nothing chosen yet) and "Change" (a choice exists) are the same button that changes its word with its state; that difference means something and should stay. The rest are the same job under other names: "Choose again" in the creation wizard. "Edit" and "Pick" are not button words anywhere on the sheet (the first text scan found code names and a select’s id, not buttons).
groups.why: One word for "reopen what I picked". Keep "Choose…" only for the very first choice. The spoken name should start with the word on the button: today nine kinds of Advantage card have a button that says "Change" or "Choose…" but is announced as "Configure {thing}", which does not match what a voice-control user would say.

groups.job: Remove an entry (a skill, an Advantage, an item, a weapon, an emphasis) from the character, or erase a saved character or book from this device.
groups.recommended_word: Remove (visible ✕ stays)  ·  Delete for saved characters and books
groups.differences_carry_meaning: Yes, and it should stay: "Remove" takes an entry off this sheet; "Delete" erases a saved character or a Library book from the device for good. Those are different acts. The visible ✕ is a picture of Remove. The problem is only the spoken name: on the test character {x_instances} ✕ buttons on rows are announced as just "✕" (a few carry a tooltip "Remove", which a screen reader does not use when the button has text).
groups.why: Two words for two different acts, kept. Every ✕ on a row gets a spoken name that says what it removes.
other_words_offered: Keep the ✕ with no spoken name

groups.plain: The ✕ in the corner of a window
groups.job: Close a window from its top corner.
groups.recommended_spoken: Close {window name}  (read-only windows)  ·  Cancel {window name}  (windows holding a choice)
groups.differences_carry_meaning: Yes. Today the corner ✕ has a tooltip "Close" on 10 windows (dice tray, roll result, skill information, untrained skills, the information windows, spell scrolls, arrows, Void and wound information) and "Cancel" on 4: the roll preview, the choice window behind Choose… and Change, the spell Element picker, and the one shared question-and-message window that every alert and every "i" text uses. That last one says "Cancel" even when it only shows a message (43 of its 75 calls are messages, such as the Kiho rules, Affinity and Weapon Info). A Close/Cancel difference can mean something (Cancel when the window holds a choice not yet kept, Close when it only shows you something); today it does not follow that.
groups.why: Keep the Close/Cancel difference, apply it by what the window is, and move it from a tooltip into the spoken name (a button with text ✕ is announced as "✕" today; only Quick Access and History say "Close").

groups.plain: The buttons at the foot of a window
groups.job: Answer or dismiss a window: leave it, keep what you chose, or acknowledge a message.
groups.recommended_word: Message: OK  ·  Yes: Confirm (or the action’s own name)  ·  No: Cancel  ·  Done where changes apply as you go
groups.differences_carry_meaning: Mostly yes. Cancel (discard) and Confirm (keep) mean different things and should stay. "Done" (changes already applied as you go) is different from "Confirm" (applied at the end): keep both. What does not carry meaning is three words for dismissing a plain message: "OK" (38 calls), "Got it" (5) and, in a few windows, "Close". Plain yes buttons also vary: "OK" (6), "Yes" (1), "Confirm" (2). Named actions ("Delete", "Discard it", "Replace", "Leave", …) are good: they say what happens.
groups.why: Three plain words cover every window, and the named actions stay. "Got it" → "OK", plain "Yes"/"OK" in a question → "Confirm", plain "No" → "Cancel".

groups.job: Roll all or part of a roll again.
groups.differences_carry_meaning: In part. The source named in the button (Luck, Kakita, Dark Paragon, an Emphasis) tells the player whose rule applies, which is useful. "GM invokes Unlucky" is not a choice the player makes, so it should read differently. groups.why: One spelling and one pattern for the rerolls a player chooses; keep "GM invokes Unlucky" and "Add Sun Tao’s die" (an added die, not a reroll) as they are.

groups.job: Add an entry to a list on the sheet.
